source.snippet: I've been doing a bit of freelance work on the side of my normal job and made around £900 from it this tax year. I keep seeing people mention a £1,000 trading allowance... Is the £1,000 based on what I got paid, or what's left after expenses? I had just under £900 come in but spent around £200 on software tools and equipment for the work.

problem_statement: UK-based side-income earners and early-stage freelancers are confused about HMRC tax thresholds (trading allowance vs. net profit), leading to anxiety about compliance, under- or over-reporting, and inability to make confident decisions about growing their freelance income.
target_segment: UK-based employed professionals earning side income (freelance, gig work) below £5,000/year who lack accountant support
notes: Buyer context: person with real money at stake (£900 income, £200 in expenses, potential HMRC penalty risk). High anxiety = willingness to pay for clarity. This is a recurring question cluster (many similar questions on Money SE, Reddit r/UKPersonalFinance). Opportunity: a low-cost UK-specific tax clarity tool for side-hustlers—a structured Q&A / decision-tree that outputs a plain-English verdict on whether they need to self-assess, with upsell to affordable accountant referral. Competing products (TaxScouts, GoSimpleTax) exist but at higher price points.
